title: Image loading and caching
summary: A good image loader checks memory cache, then disk cache, then network; decodes and downsamples off the main thread; dedupes duplicate requests; and cancels loads for cells that scroll away.
body: **In simple words:** Images are the heaviest thing in most apps. Loading them well means: do not download twice, do not decode on main, do not keep huge bitmaps in memory, and do not waste work on cells already off screen.

**The pipeline:** request(url, targetSize) → memory cache (decoded, ready to draw) → disk cache (compressed file) → network download → decode + downsample on a background thread → store in both caches → set on the view if it still wants this URL.

**Two cache levels:** memory cache (`NSCache` with a cost limit, cleared under pressure) holds decoded images for instant display. Disk cache (files in `Caches/`, LRU eviction by size/age) avoids re-downloading. `URLCache` can also serve as an HTTP-level disk cache if the server sends cache headers.
**Dedupe and cancel:** if 3 cells ask for the same URL, run one download and share it. When a cell is reused, cancel its previous request so it does not show the wrong image.
**Prefetch:** start loads for rows about to appear (`prefetchItemsAt`), cancel when they no longer will.
**Libraries:** Kingfisher, Nuke, SDWebImage do all this. In an interview, explain the design even if you would use a library. See also the System Design page "Image loading library".
keyPoints: Memory cache (decoded, NSCache) → disk cache (compressed) → network.
Decode and downsample off main to the displayed pixel size.
Deduplicate in-flight requests; cancel on cell reuse.
Prefetch upcoming rows; respect Low Data Mode for large images.
Key cache by URL + target size so thumbnails and full images do not clash.

code.caption: Minimal async image loader

mistakes: Decoding images on the main thread in `cellForRowAt`.
Not cancelling loads on reuse, causing flicker and wrong images.
followups: **How would you size the memory cache?** As a cost in bytes of decoded pixels (e.g. 10-20% of available memory), not as an item count.
**What format would you request?** Server-resized images in modern formats (HEIC/WebP/AVIF) at the needed size; this saves bandwidth and decode time.
